bible_refs.note: Τεκνία μου, οὓς πάλιν ὠδίνω ἄχρις οὗ μορφωθῇ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν mirrors Paul's 'my little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you'
Οὐ γὰρ ἐν παλαιότητι γράμματος, ἀλλ' ἐν καινό τητι πνεύματος περιπατεῖν corresponds to 'we serve in newness of spirit, and not in oldness of the letter'
∆ύναται γὰρ οὐδεὶς, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος φωνὴν, δυσὶ δουλεύειν κυρίοις is a verbatim citation of 'No one can serve two masters' from the Savior's voice
Ὁ ἀγαπῶν με, τὰς ἐντολάς μου τηρεῖ.
Οἱ γὰρ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τὴν σάρκα ἐσταύρωσαν σὺν τοῖς παθήμασι καὶ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις.
νεκροῦντes τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τουτέστι πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν, καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν
παριστάντες δὲ μᾶλλον ἑαυτοὺς εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας
καὶ θυσίαν ὥσπερ τινὰ πνευματικὴν οἰκείαν ἀνατι θέντες ζωὴν τῷ φιλαρέτῳ Θεῷ
Ἐξαπόστειλον τὸν λαόν μου, ἵνα μοι δουλεύσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἐρή μῳ matches Exodus 5:1 LXX

choices.why: Present active indicative of ὠδίνω with πάλιν conveying repeated intensitive effort, not merely 'I suffer' but birth pangs toward spiritual formation
Aorist passive subjunctive of μορφόω after ἄχρις οὗ indicating goal of the travail, not passive 'you are shaped' but Christ taking shape inwardly
Dative of manner after ἐν contrasting with παλαιότητι γράμματος, πνεῦμα here as inner regenerative principle not mere 'wind' or 'breath'

choices.english: our own mind as if nerve-stretched
choices.why: Contextual rendering of OCR-corrupted νοῦν ὡς ἁπάσης ἁγνείας ἡμῖν ἐσομένην as νοῦν ὡς νεῦρατα σविदेशी, interpreting ἁγνείας as metaphorical tension, not literal purity state
In context of ἀνακεῖσθαι (to lie upon, dedicate), λατρεῖα denotes solemn service due to Christ alone, not generic 'service' or 'ministry'

choices.term: ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει, καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται, καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει.
choices.english: For either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other.
choices.why: This is a clear presentation of the exclusive choice between two masters, using antithetical parallelism characteristic of Jesus' teaching in Matthew 6:24/Luke 16:13. The Greek 'ἠ... ἠ...' construction forces the either/or dilemma, which I preserved in English with 'For either... or...' to maintain the logical force.
rejected: Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will stick with one and reject the other.
He will either hate one and love the other, or he will cling to one and scorn the other.

choices.term: Παραιτητέον οὖν ἄρα τὸν οὐκ ὄντα δεσπότην, φημὶ δὴ τὸν Σατανᾶν
choices.english: Therefore, we must reject the non-existing master, I mean Satan,
choices.why: The Greek uses the impersonal necessity 'παραιτητέον' (must be rejected) with 'οὖν ἄρα' (therefore thus) drawing a conclusion. 'Φημὶ δὴ' is an emphatic clarification ('I mean'). I rendered this as 'Therefore, we must reject... I mean Satan' to preserve the rhetorical force and parenthetical clarification while making the impersonal construction natural in English.
rejected: It is necessary therefore to reject the non-existing master, that is, Satan.
We must then reject the master who does not exist, namely Satan.

choices.term: Ὁ ἀγαπῶν με, τὰς ἐντολάς μου τηρεῖ.
choices.english: The one who loves me keeps my commandments.
choices.why: This is a direct quote of Jesus' words (John 14:15, 21, 23; 15:10). The Greek uses the present participle 'ἀγαπῶν' (loving) with future 'τηρεῖ' (keeps), indicating a characteristic action. I rendered it as a simple present tense relative clause in English to match the gnomic, timeless truth being expressed, which is the natural way to convey this in English while preserving the meaning.
rejected: Whoever loves me, he keeps my commandments.
The loving one of me observes my commands.

choices.term: νεκροῦντες τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τουτέστι πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακὴν, καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν
choices.english: mortifying the members that are upon the earth, namely fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed.
choices.why: The Greek 'νεκροῦντες' (mortifying) is a present participle indicating ongoing action. 'Τ Ground' is an appositional clarification ('namely'). I rendered this as 'mortifying... namely' to preserve the participial phrase and the explanatory apposition, which matches Paul's language in Colossians 3:5 where he lists these exact sins as 'earthly members'.
rejected: Putting to death the earthly members: fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed.
Killing off the bodily parts that are on the earth, that is to say, sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desire, and greed.

choices.term: παριστάντες δὲ μᾶλλον ἑαυτοὺς εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καὶ θυσίαν ὥσπερ τινὰ πνευματικὴν οἰκείαν ἀνατι θέντες ζωὴν τῷ φιλαρέτῳ Θεῷ.
choices.english: Presenting ourselves rather as a fragrance of sweet smell, according to what is written, and setting up a spiritual sacrifice, as it were, we give life to the God who loves virtue.
choices.why: The Greek 'παριστάντες' (presenting) is a present participle showing concurrent action with the main verb. 'Εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας' is a prepositional phrase meaning 'into a fragrance of sweet smell' (cf. Ephesians 5:2, Philippians 4:18). 'Ωσπερ τινὰ' means 'as it were' or 'like a sort of'. I rendered this as a participle phrase 'Presenting ourselves rather as...' followed by 'and setting up...' to show the two concurrent actions, then completed the thought with 'we give life to...' to match the Greek structure where the participles lead to the main idea.
rejected: Presenting ourselves more as a fragrance of sweet smell according to what is written, and setting up a spiritual sacrifice like a certain one, we give life to the God who loves virtue.
We present ourselves as a sweet-smelling offering, as Scripture says, and we establish a spiritual sacrifice, thereby giving life to the God who loves what is good.

choices.why: The participle δαπανωμένους from δαπναóω means 'wasted' or 'exhausted by labor', fitting the context of oppressed slaves; 'worn out' is a natural English equivalent.
ἀνακομίζειν literally means 'to bring back' or 'recover', and here God purposes to restore Israel’s ancient freedom; 'bring back' preserves the spatial and restorative sense.

choices.english: to renounce and to finish completely
choices.why: The双动词 construction ἀποσχέσθαι (to renounce, abstain from) and καταλῆξαι (to finish, make an end of) together express a full abandonment of labor; the rendering captures both aspects without omission.

pass_b_english: My children, I am again in the pains of labor for you until Christ is inwardly formed in your souls.
This formation of Christ within you happens in no other way than through a faith without reproach and a way of life shaped by the gospel.
For we do not walk by the outward oldness of the written code, but by the inward newness that comes from the Spirit, especially those of you who are making your way toward God.

I believe this also works effectively within us when we prepare our minds for every good deed, stretching them taut like nerves, so that our very thoughts may become pure and undistorted, not monstrous or warped.

In this state we willingly accept this most blessed fast, observing it with measured moderation in our eating, free from useless curiosity about what we may eat, and keeping our partaking of food simple and undistracted, so that we may also sharpen the eye of our understanding.
Yet we know well that the toil of the flesh alone does not bring holiness to our souls, nor does mere abstinence suffice to display true virtue before others.
True holiness requires the purity that comes from righteous actions joined with the dignity of a holy life, and it is sustained by the joyful witness of those who truly accomplish the fast.
Therefore I maintain, and indeed I say more strongly, that what is most necessary is to give ourselves completely and wholly to the worship of Christ, holding nothing back from that devotion.

Let us not turn away in any direction from the straight path, abandoning the firm way by which one walks toward God, to be carried off course instead, and let us not foolishly complete our end in what appears to the devil as reasonable, for as the Savior himself said, no one is able to serve two masters.
